meta.title: Riptide: the free, open-source download manager for Windows
meta.description: Free, open-source download manager for Windows. Resumes from the exact byte, verified with SHA-256. No accounts, no telemetry, no ads. Arabic and English.
meta.ogAlt: Riptide: the download manager that pulls harder

hero.title: The download manager that pulls harder.
hero.lead: Riptide splits each file across many connections, resumes from the exact byte after a pause, a crash or a power cut, and verifies the result with SHA-256. Free and open source, for Windows.
hero.note: Free alpha preview, 64-bit, no admin rights needed. It is an early build and it changes often.
hero.line: No accounts. No telemetry. No ads.
hero.visualLabel: Animated illustration: segment stripes flow like a current and assemble into a completed download bar.

download.title: Download the alpha preview
download.badge: Alpha preview — Windows 10/11, 64-bit, no admin rights needed
download.lead: Pick the installer for a per-user setup that never asks for elevation, or the portable zip to run Riptide from any folder.
download.requirements: Requirements: Windows 10 / 11, x64. WebView2 (included in Windows).
download.note: Alpha means early: the build changes often and rough edges are expected. Each release lists SHA-256 checksums for both files. If something breaks, tell us below.

extension.title: Browser extension
extension.lead: The extension catches downloads in the browser and hands them to the app, so every file gets the same segmented, verified transfer. It also puts a Riptide button on download links.
extension.sub: Until the store listings are live, load the extension from the repository. It works in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

why.title: Why Riptide
why.lead: Most download managers are a decade of features behind a nag screen. Riptide is a new engine built around a handful of rules it cannot skip.

items.title: Pulls harder
items.text: A file is split into segments and fetched over many connections at once. When one connection finishes early it takes half of the largest segment left, so the link stays full to the last byte.

items.title: Byte-exact or nothing
items.text: A download is complete only when every segment is on disk, the server still serves the same version of the file, and the checksum you gave matches. Riptide never splices bytes from two versions of a file.

items.title: Survives anything
items.text: Progress is committed to a local SQLite database at least once a second. Kill the process or pull the plug and every download resumes from the exact byte. If the server changed the file meanwhile, Riptide starts over instead of handing you a corrupt one.

items.title: Video pages too
items.text: Paste a YouTube, Vimeo or other video page and Riptide fetches it through bundled yt-dlp, into the same list as every other download. It is in the main branch and ships in the next alpha.

items.title: Queues with schedules
items.text: The queue engine and the per-queue scheduler are finished and tested. The screens that control them are still being built, so they are not in any release yet.

items.title: Arabic and English, for real
items.text: Both languages everywhere, detected automatically and switchable live, with a fully mirrored right-to-left layout. Arabic file names from servers land on disk with the right name.

items.title: Nothing to trust
items.text: Server file names are sanitised, redirects are capped at 20, credentials never leave the site they were captured for, and TLS verification is on. Secrets live in their own table and are wiped when a download ends.

items.title: No admin, no accounts, no ads, no telemetry
items.text: A per-user install that never asks for elevation. Your data stays on your machine, and the only network traffic is your downloads.

items.title: A list that stays fast
items.text: Dense, keyboard-friendly, smooth with a thousand items. Dark or light, and it respects the reduced-motion setting.

vs.title: The open-source alternative to IDM
vs.lead: Internet Download Manager set the bar for segmented downloads on Windows. Riptide keeps the bar and drops the license, the reminders and the closed source.

how.title: How a download happens
how.lead: Four moves, repeated for every file. Each one is a rule the engine cannot skip.

steps.title: Probe
steps.text: Before a single byte is downloaded, Riptide asks the server about the file: its size, its name, whether it accepts ranges, and a validator (ETag or Last-Modified) that pins the exact version.

steps.title: Split
steps.text: The file is divided into equal segments, one per connection, and the final size is preallocated on disk so every segment writes straight into its own place.

steps.title: Steal
steps.text: When a connection finishes early it takes half of the largest remaining segment from a slower one. No connection sits idle while there are bytes left.

steps.title: Checkpoint, verify, rename
steps.text: Progress is committed to a local database at least once a second. When the last byte lands, the validator is checked again, the checksum is computed, and the .rtpart file is renamed into place.

oss.title: Open source, nothing to hide
oss.text: The desktop app, the command-line client and the IPC crate are licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. The engine crates are dual-licensed MIT or Apache-2.0, so anyone can build on them. There is no telemetry, no account and no advertising: the only network traffic is your downloads.
oss.public: Riptide is built in public. Every change lands on GitHub first, and so does every report, rating and release note.
oss.badgeNote: These are plain links. This page loads nothing from third parties, so there is no badge service to call.

items.a: Yes. Riptide is free and open source, and will stay that way. There is no paid tier, no license key and no trial.
Yes, as an alpha preview for Windows 10 / 11 (64-bit): a per-user installer that needs no admin rights, or a portable zip. It is an early build that changes often, so expect rough edges.

items.q: Does it work with my browser?
items.a: There is an extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox that catches downloads and hands them to the app. Store listings for Chrome and Edge are coming soon; until then you load it from the GitHub repository.
Windows first. The engine itself is portable Rust with no Windows-only code in it, so other platforms can follow, but there is no date for that.
Everything happens in the open on GitHub: commits, issues, releases and the README. Star or watch the repository.
Yes. Issues, bug reports and pull requests are welcome on GitHub. Read the README first; it explains how to build from source and which checks every change must pass.

items.q: How do I report a bug or leave a review?
items.a: Use the Feedback section above. Bug reports, feature requests and reviews each have their own GitHub form, and security problems go through private reporting.
Video pages such as YouTube and Vimeo work through bundled yt-dlp in the main branch and will ship in the next alpha. Queues with schedules come after that: the engine is done, the screens are not.

meta.title: Privacy policy · Riptide
meta.description: Riptide and its browser extension collect nothing: no telemetry, no accounts, no analytics. What stays on your computer and the few network requests Riptide makes.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.updated: Last updated: 19 October 2026. Applies to the Riptide desktop app, the Riptide CLI, the Riptide browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox, and this website.
privacy.lede: Short version: Riptide collects nothing. There is no telemetry, no analytics, no account and no advertising. Your downloads, settings and history stay on your computer, and nobody, including the people who make Riptide, receives any of it.

paras: Nothing. Riptide has no server of its own. The app, the CLI and the extension do not send usage statistics, crash reports, identifiers or any other information to us or to anyone else.
Riptide does not use accounts, so there is no sign-up, no e-mail address and no profile.

The download list, its progress and your settings are kept in a local database in your user profile (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Riptide on Windows). Log files are written to the same folder; the addresses in them have their query strings removed and cookies, passwords and authorization headers are never written to them.
You can delete any of this at any time by removing downloads from the list or by deleting the folder.
Riptide connects to the servers of the files you choose to download, and to nothing else on your behalf.

The only request it makes on its own is an optional check for a new version against GitHub Releases (github.com). It sends nothing about you beyond what any web request carries, such as your IP address, and it can be turned off in Settings. GitHub's own privacy statement applies to that request.

The extension's only job is to hand downloads from your browser to the Riptide app on the same computer. It talks to the app through the browser's Native Messaging channel; it has no network access of its own, loads no remote code and contains no analytics.

When it hands over a download it passes the download address, the suggested file name, the referring page and the browser's user agent to the local app. Your rules and language choice are saved in the browser's extension storage and never leave the browser.

Some downloads only work when you are signed in. For those, the extension reads the browser's cookies for the address being downloaded, and only that address, and passes them to the local Riptide app.

Riptide sends those cookies only to the same site they belong to, for that one download, and never to another site, including after a redirect to a different origin. They are kept in a separate local table while the download is in progress, are never written to logs, and are deleted as soon as the download completes or is removed.

This site is a set of static pages hosted on GitHub Pages. It uses no cookies, no analytics and no trackers, and it loads nothing from third parties: fonts, images and scripts come from the same origin. The only thing it stores is your light or dark theme choice, in your own browser. GitHub may keep ordinary server logs under its own privacy policy.
The Feedback section links to GitHub issue forms. What you write there is public on GitHub and governed by GitHub's terms and privacy statement; this site never sees it.

Because we receive no data, we have nothing to share, sell or transfer, and nothing is used for advertising, credit decisions or any purpose other than your downloads. Riptide is not directed at children and collects no information from anyone.

If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new date, and the history of the page is public in the source repository. Questions are welcome as an issue on GitHub at github.com/LayanJarrar1/Riptide/issues.

feedback.title: Tell us what happened
feedback.lead: Riptide is in alpha, so your reports decide what gets fixed first. Everything goes through GitHub issues: public, searchable and tracked until it is closed.

cards.title: Report a problem
cards.text: A download failed, a file did not match its checksum, the app crashed. The form asks for your Riptide and Windows versions and the log lines that matter.

cards.title: Suggest a feature
cards.text: Describe the problem you want solved before the solution you have in mind. We read every request and answer yes, not yet or no, with a reason.

cards.title: Leave a review
cards.text: Rate Riptide from 1 to 5 and tell us what you used it for, what worked and what did not. A low rating with detail helps more than a high one without.

cards.title: Report a security issue
cards.text: Do not open a public issue. Use GitHub's private reporting, described in SECURITY.md, so a fix can ship before the details are public.

feedback.whyTitle: Why GitHub, and no form here
feedback.why: Public reports let other people find the same problem, add detail and see when it is fixed. You need a free GitHub account. This site has no form of its own, no analytics and no tracking scripts, so there is nothing here that could collect your message.
